findings.claim: A missing `)` in an if condition is reported on the wrong line. With `if (cents < 0 {` on line 7, the editor shows "Error, line 10: ')' expected. Every ( needs a matching ): check the brackets on line 10." Line 10 is `this.cents = cents;`, and its brackets are balanced. By 14.9 the header is `if ( Expression ) Statement`, so the `)` is missing before the `{` on line 7, and that is the line to change. A single-line case (a missing `)` inside one return statement) is reported on its own line, so only the header-plus-block shape is affected. Rated medium: a missing `)` before `{` is a common beginner slip, the message sends the learner to a line that is already correct, and the line reported is part of simulator fidelity. Reproduced headless in Chromium (Playwright) against the current bytes at c0066ed8; no JDK is installed, so javac was not run and its exact wording is not asserted.
findings.recommendation: When the statement pass meets an unclosed `(` in an if, for or while header and then reaches the `{` that opens its body (or a depth-0 `;`), report "')' expected" at after() of the token before that `{`/`;`, so the line shown is the header line. Never report it at the end of the enclosing body.

location.selector: #cf-3 practice editor (shared engine enum body reader and plain() message)

findings.claim: When a field comes before the constants (`enum Coin {` / `private final int cents;` / `PENNY(1), NICKEL(5), DIME(10), QUARTER(25);`), the editor now says "Error, line 1: ',', '}', or ';' expected. The list of constants ends with a semicolon (;): add it at the end of line 1." Line 1 is `enum Coin {`. By the 8.9.1 grammar, constants must come before body declarations. Following the advice (`enum Coin {;`) makes the field legal but turns the constant line into a member that does not parse, so the real fix, moving the constants first, is never named. Rated low: the starter already puts the constants first. Reproduced headless in Chromium (Playwright) against the current bytes at c0066ed8; no JDK is installed, so javac was not run and its exact wording is not asserted.
findings.recommendation: When the token after `{` in an enum body is a modifier or type rather than a constant name, say "The constants come first in an enum, before fields, constructors and methods", instead of advising a semicolon on the enum line.
